A zone you can actually reach and a zone the seekers find expensive to reach are opposite things. One that scores well on both is genuinely rare — and it is what you are shopping for below.

The playbook for this map

How to play this map

Everything below follows from the official rules applied to this particular network — each tip names the clause it comes from, and tips whose precondition does not hold here have been left out.

7 things to do differently on this map, in the order they matter.

  1. Spend the whole 60 minutes

    Your hiding window is the only free movement you get. Wherever you are standing when the timer ends is your zone, so plan the ride, not just the destination — and check the travel time in the dossier before you commit to a zone.

    Hiding Zones — “if the hiding period ends and you're somewhere else, then that's where your hiding zone is.”

  2. Scope your endgame spot early, then wander

    Inside your 0.25 mi circle you can shop, eat and sightsee — but the moment a seeker walks in off transit you freeze where you stand. Know exactly where you will be standing, and pre-take the photos you can, so a photo timer never forces you to sprint.

    Hiding Spots — the spot is final the moment the end game starts.

  3. Parks are the best-in-class final spot

    Publicly accessible at all hours, no risk of being asked to leave, and their path networks satisfy the ten-feet-of-a-mapped-path rule. This map has 1,395 of them. A large park is doubly useful: “nearest park” measures to the map icon, so you can be standing in one park and truthfully name a different one.

    Hiding Spots — publicly accessible during all game hours; Matching — measure to the map icon.

  4. Businesses are a mid-round tool, not a hiding spot

    The rulebook warns against stores and businesses as final spots — loitering draws attention and opening hours rarely cover all game hours. Use them for a bathroom, food and warmth during the middle of the round, then be somewhere public when the endgame starts.

    Hiding Spots — “we'd suggest avoiding stores or other businesses.”

  5. Respect the tentacle categories

    The live tentacle categories here are Hospitals Within 1 Mile, Libraries Within 1 Mile, Movie Theaters Within 1 Mile, Museums Within 1 Mile. The radius is measured from the seekers, not from you, so a target well outside your zone can still be the name you have to give. A zone where the category is absent or ambiguous blunts the whole family — and a null answer still pays you a card draw.

    Tentacle Questions — 1-mile reach in a MEDIUM game.

  6. Radar targets you, not your zone

    If the ring clips your circle but not your body, the honest answer is no. Stand on the far side of your 0.25 mi disc from the seekers' likely approach — the simulator above shows exactly which zones turn amber, and amber is the band where standing in the right half of your own circle changes the answer.

    Radar Questions — the answer is about your location, not your zone.

  7. Build the deck to end the round holding time

    Time bonuses only count if they are in your hand when you are caught. Aim for roughly half bonuses, a quarter powerups, a quarter curses — and remember that Move costs your entire hand, reveals your original station, and cannot be played in the end game.

    The Hider Deck — six-card hand limit; Powerups — Move.

Six axes, one hundred points

How zones are scored

Every zone is scored the same way, from the feed and from OpenStreetMap. Nothing here is a matter of taste: each axis is a list of named metrics with published thresholds, and every zone's dossier shows which of them it earned. Open an axis for its metrics and the rulebook clause behind it.

Every one of the 1,204 zones sat the same six-axis exam, and every point it earned is listed in its own dossier.
How well you blend in IR Information resistance 30.0 pt

How many other zones give the seekers the same answers you do. A zone whose answer vector is shared with many others survives questioning; a zone with a unique answer vector is named by one cheap question.

On this map, asking “Restaurant Interior” leaves on average 603 of 1,204 zones still standing.

MetricUnitWorthWhere it comes from
IR1 Zones sharing your answers to the map's best questionsshare12.0 pt Our call
IR2 Worst single question, per card it costs0–110.0 pt Our call
IR3 Average anonymity across every live question0–18.0 pt Our call

Rulebook: Seeking — every question is answered truthfully, so the only defence is being indistinguishable.

How easy it is to get there R Reach 15.0 pt

Whether you can actually get here inside the hiding period, and how many changes it costs.

Reach and Exposure pull against each other on purpose, and that tension is the whole game. R1 rewards a zone you can actually get to inside the hiding period; X3 rewards a zone the seekers find expensive to reach. A zone that scores well on both is genuinely rare, and it is what you are shopping for below.
MetricUnitWorthWhere it comes from
R1 Travel time from the start, ÷ the hiding periodratio9.0 pt From the rules
R2 Transfers on the best journeychanges6.0 pt Our call

Rulebook: Hiding Zones — “if the hiding period ends and you're somewhere else, then that's where your hiding zone is.”

How good the buses are S Service 15.0 pt

Onward departures, the gap between them, and how much margin you have on the last ride out of the zone.

MetricUnitWorthWhere it comes from
S1 Distinct routes inside the zoneroutes6.0 pt From the rules
S2 Minutes of margin on the last ride homemin5.0 pt Our call
S3 Median gap between departures from the zonemin4.0 pt From the rules

Rulebook: Curses & powerups — Move costs your whole hand and needs a bus to exist.

Places you can legally freeze at the end E Endgame spots 15.0 pt

Publicly-accessible places inside the circle where you can legally freeze when a seeker walks in, and whether they are clustered or scattered.

MetricUnitWorthWhere it comes from
E1 Candidate legal hiding spotsweighted count8.0 pt Our call
E2 Separate spot clustersclusters4.0 pt From the rules
E3 Spots enclosed by a park, plaza or campusshare3.0 pt Our call

Rulebook: Hiding Spots — publicly accessible during all game hours, within 10 ft of a mapped path.

What's nearby A Amenities 15.0 pt

A bathroom you can use, food and water, and shelter — the things that decide whether you can sit here for hours.

MetricUnitWorthWhere it comes from
A1 A bathroom you can actually use0–16.0 pt From the rules
A2 Food and water inside the circleplaces5.0 pt From the rules
A3 Shelter from the weatherscore4.0 pt Our call

Rulebook: Hiding — “you're free to do whatever you like”, for as long as it takes.

How hard you are to reach X Exposure 10.0 pt

Map-edge and radar exposure, how many neighbouring zones share your patch, and how expensive you are for the seekers to reach.

Reach and Exposure pull against each other on purpose, and that tension is the whole game. R1 rewards a zone you can actually get to inside the hiding period; X3 rewards a zone the seekers find expensive to reach. A zone that scores well on both is genuinely rare, and it is what you are shopping for below.
MetricUnitWorthWhere it comes from
X1 Share of your circle outside the bordershare4.0 pt Our call
X2 Other zones within 1.00 mizones3.0 pt Our call
X3 Seeker travel cost to reach you, ÷ T90ratio3.0 pt Measured

Rulebook: Radar Questions — an outlier is pinned by one question; Measuring — distance from the seekers is itself information.

What produced these rankings

Method & parameters

Everything on this page was produced from Chicago Transit Authority's published timetable and from OpenStreetMap, for a MEDIUM game starting at Michigan & Washington.
ParameterValue
Zones scored1,204
Zone radius0.25 mi
Game sizeMEDIUM (inferred)
Hiding period60 min
Round startMichigan & Washington
Departure09:00:00
Day shownWeekday
Live questions52 of 71
FeedChicago Transit Authority —
Analysis dateTue 7 Jul 2026
